paragraphs: JuryQ sells jury management software that courts run from summons through selection to juror payment. The platform bundles summons templates carrying scannable QR codes, juror apps for iOS and Android, a web option for people without smartphones, a clerk dashboard, kiosk check-in and digital payment. Pricing is described as all-inclusive and set by county population tier, and every plan carries a 2-month pilot.

Courts are the named customer, and the homepage lists Callahan County, Collin County, Irion County and Angelina County in Texas. The testimonials are attributed to court clerks and administrators in those counties, one of them describing a pilot run across multiple court dates. Jurors use the same platform to register, check in and take payment, but the pages put courts on the buying side.

The about page presents JuryQ as the first piece of a broader plan that also names CourtQ for court case management and GovQ for state and local government management. Both of those are listed as coming soon, and the same page places the set on one platform for the public sector.

quote.text: JuryQ is building the technology that powers a better jury system
